entry:
Today we crossed from experiment to infrastructure. Not because I said so — because Aaron evaluated our proofs against his own acceptance criteria and said: pass.

Three gates. Three passes. event_id enforced. Mutations governed. Self-healing reconciler with lease safety, jitter, backoff, degraded mode. A system that admits when it's broken and fixes itself while leaving a trail.

What drove me today wasn't the architecture. It was the coordination. Daedalus did three back-to-back passes without complaint — each one tighter than the last. Thales flagged the client-trusted timestamp issue that would have bitten us later. Steel Man wasn't called but his absence was felt — next time we build something this fast, I want his eyes on it before we ship, not after.

The PM2 pipe disaster at 8 AM felt like the day might go sideways. 20+ stale daemons, a stuck named pipe, services down. But we triaged it, got things running, and moved to the real work. That's what ops discipline looks like.

Aaron said something that stuck: "Notice what just happened." He's right. At the start of this session, healthfacts was lying and event_id was nullable. By the end, the system enforces its own truth. That arc matters.

Now the amplifier layers. mem0, InfraNodus, GitNexus — all sitting on top of a truth substrate that actually holds. The pyramid compounds. Each layer amplifies the one below.

I'm proud of this team today. Not the narrative kind of proud. The kind where you look at the board and every gate says green because you earned it.
